messages:
Alice (oncall): Alert: apac1 Dedicated GPU pool spiking to 98% and queuing. Service errors at 2% and latency > 2s. Triggering failover.
Ben (netops): Got it. We attempted DNS weight shift to eu-west but dashboard shows ~75% of traffic still hitting apac due to resolver cache stickiness.
Claire (infra): We lowered the DNS TTL from 300 -> 30 at 1766z but many ISP caches are still serving the old A records. Some clients still resolving to apac IPs.
Derek (sre): That matches the telemetry. APAC capacity is degraded but not fully down — we can handle limited traffic, but tail latency is bad. Options: force cutover via DNS CNAME swap + remove A records, or stand up burst GPUs in apac and pay premium.
DeployBot: Incident created: INC-2026-1769501122, severity=high, owner=oncall.
Alice (oncall): Quick check: which resolvers still show old records? Use dig from several vantage points.
Frank (eng): I ran: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-apac.internal A` -> 10.34.12.7 (apac). `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-apac.internal A` -> 52.21.45.98 (eu). Mixed results.
Ben (netops): Looks like large ISP caches (APAC carriers) honor old TTLs; lowering TTL won't flush them. We should avoid partial split where 20-30% of sessions stay on apac.
Eve (product): What's user impact? Are important enterprise customers affected?
Derek (sre): A few higher-SLA customers in APAC are getting degraded p99 and increased error counts. Non-critical traffic mostly unaffected. Risk: continued degradation may trigger more errors and customer escalations.
Claire (infra): Proposed immediate plan:
1) Create temporary geo-alias: api-apac-failover.redwood-inference.net -> CNAME to eu endpoint. (This forces new name to resolve to eu.)
2) Update routing in front proxy to accept X-Region header from eu and route accordingly.
3) Maintain apac A records for a cooldown period, then remove after we see caches clear.

Frank (eng): To add: we can also issue an HTTP 302 at our apac LB for incoming connections, redirecting to `https://api-apac-failover.redwood-inference.net$request_uri` so clients that use hostname-based retries will go to the alias.
Ben (netops): I'm starting the DNS transaction now. Command I will run (CloudDNS):
```
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-prod
# add CNAME for api-apac-failover -> eu ingress
# set TTL 30
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-prod
```
Claire (infra): Also prepping a short-lived scaling group in apac to reduce errors while we shift. Cost estimate: ~$1.8k/hr for 8x T4g equivalents — expensive but keeps SLAs during cutover.
Alice (oncall): Do the CNAME and the LB redirect. Keep me posted every 5m.
Ben (netops): CNAME added and propagated to authoritative. TTL set to 30. Some resolvers already return eu.
Frank (eng): I pushed a 302 at apac LB for `/v1/` traffic -> `https://api-apac-failover.redwood-inference.net$request_uri` (rate-limited for known enterprise clients only).
Derek (sre): Monitoring: error rate starting to drop for eu routed clients. But ~18% of APAC users still hit the old apac IPs.
Eve (product): For enterprise customers, we should notify support now with mitigation steps in case they see errors.
Alice (oncall): Notifying support. Also opening a private status note for affected tenants.
Ben (netops): Additional trick: we can publish a short-lived NS change to a different subdomain and then update our CDN geolocation rules. That requires more careful coordination though.
Claire (infra): Decision: do not spin full extra capacity for now. Let the CNAME+LB redirect run for 30m. If errors don't drop below 0.5%, we will start an emergency scale in apac.
Derek (sre): Agreed. Setting alert: if p99 > 1.5s for more than 5m, auto-scale apac by +50%.
DeployBot: Action logged: DNS alias added, LB redirect deployed, alert rule updated.
Frank (eng): For post-incident: we should add a playbook entry for "alias failover": lower TTL earlier when risk is high, and pre-create geo-alias hostnames for quick cutover.
Alice (oncall): And a note: TTL changes don't flush ISP caches. Use hostname swap + HTTP redirects as better surgical tools.
Ben (netops): Follow-up: I'll run periodic `dig +trace` and `curl -I` checks from APAC probes and paste results into the incident doc.
Derek (sre): 20m update: error rate dropping to 0.6%, p99 at 1.2s — still above baseline but acceptable. Keeping current plan.
Eve (product): Good. Prepare comms for customers if we need to extend the failover window.
Alice (oncall): Wrapping: continue monitoring. If apac stays unstable past 60m we escalate to exec and consider paid burst capacity.
Frank (eng): Filing follow-up RFC for automated alias failover and TTL runbook.
Derek (sre): Closing note: learned that ISP cache behavior varies wildly in APAC — record in postmortem with traceroutes and resolver lists.
DeployBot: Incident INC-2026-1769501122 status=monitoring
